issues.legal_issue: When a development authority cancels a scheme after collecting payments and does not allot the promised plots, the collected money must be returned with compensatory interest.
material_facts: The applicant paid the amount demanded for a plot under a housing scheme.
The authority cancelled the scheme and did not allot the plot.
The authority had floated another scheme over the same land, as alleged by the applicant; the Court held the case was covered by its earlier ruling on the cancelled scheme.
issues.conclusion: The Commission's direction to refund the money with interest at 18% per annum was justified, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Following Ghaziabad Development Authority v. Balbir Singh (2004) 5 SCC 65, paragraph 21, the authority must return collected money with interest at 18% even if there was a genuine reason for cancelling the scheme; the interest is fair compensation where the authority is to derive substantial benefit from the land.

rule.if: consumer_appeal and scheme_cancelled and payments_collected and plot_not_allotted and authority_benefits_from_land

predicates.consumer_appeal: The matter is an appeal concerning relief granted in a consumer dispute.
predicates.scheme_cancelled: The development authority cancelled the housing scheme under which plots were to be allotted.
predicates.payments_collected: Applicants paid money to the authority for plots under the scheme.
predicates.plot_not_allotted: The authority did not allot the promised plot to the applicant.
predicates.authority_benefits_from_land: The authority stands to derive substantial benefit from the land covered by the cancelled scheme.

issues.definition: When a consumer appeal concerns a cancelled scheme for which payments were collected and plots were not allotted, and the authority stands to benefit from the land, the collected money must be returned with compensatory interest.

issues.legal_issue: An allottee cannot obtain both compensatory interest for non-allotment and a plot under the original or a later scheme as additional relief.
material_facts: The allottee applied for a plot, paid the full amount due, and received confirmation of the allotment.
The authority did not deliver possession, citing incomplete development work and a period during which a court stay prevented development.
The Commission awarded interest on the refunded amount as damages and compensation for non-allotment.
The allottee sought a plot under the original scheme or an alternate plot under a later scheme in addition to the interest.
issues.conclusion: The allottee was not entitled to both the plot and compensatory interest; the award of interest was justified, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Ghaziabad Development Authority v. Balbir Singh (2004) 5 SCC 65, including paragraph 12, interest awarded for non-allotment is damages and compensation; the claimant cannot retain that compensation while also claiming the plot as additional relief.

rule.if: consumer_appeal and full_payment_for_allotted_plot and possession_not_delivered and compensatory_interest_awarded and claimant_seeks_plot_as_additional_relief

predicates.consumer_appeal: The matter is an appeal concerning relief granted in a consumer dispute.
predicates.full_payment_for_allotted_plot: The allottee paid the full amount due for a plot that the authority had confirmed as allotted.
predicates.possession_not_delivered: The authority did not deliver possession of the allotted plot.
predicates.compensatory_interest_awarded: A consumer forum awarded interest as damages and compensation for the failure to allot or deliver the plot.
predicates.claimant_seeks_plot_as_additional_relief: The claimant sought the plot, or an alternate plot, in addition to the awarded compensatory interest.

issues.definition: Where an allottee has paid in full, has not received possession, and has been awarded compensatory interest, the allottee cannot also claim a plot as additional relief.

issues.legal_issue: Interest need not be awarded for a period when a court stay prevented the authority from carrying out development work and delivering possession.
material_facts: A court stay prevented the authority from carrying out development and construction work for a period.
The Commission relied on the authority's report that the stay prevented delivery of possession and held that no interest was payable for that period.
The Supreme Court accepted that finding, relying on its earlier decision in the same context.
issues.conclusion: The Commission's exclusion of interest for the period when the stay prevented development and delivery of possession was accepted.
issues.legal_principle: Ghaziabad Development Authority v. Balbir Singh (2004) 5 SCC 65, paragraph 25, accepted that no interest was payable for a period when a court stay prevented development work and delivery of possession.

predicates.consumer_appeal: The matter is an appeal concerning relief granted in a consumer dispute.
predicates.interest_claimed_for_non_delivery: The claimant seeks interest as compensation for the authority's failure to deliver possession.
predicates.court_stay_prevented_development_and_pos: A court stay prevented the authority from carrying out development work and delivering possession during the relevant period.

issues.definition: When a consumer appeal concerns interest for non-delivery and a court stay prevented the development and delivery, interest is not payable for the delay caused by that stay.

issues.legal_issue: A contempt petition does not survive when the related appeal order leaves no contempt matter to be determined.
material_facts: A contempt petition was pending in connection with a civil appeal.
The Court made an order in that civil appeal and consequently considered the contempt petition no longer surviving.
issues.conclusion: The contempt petition was closed as not surviving.
issues.legal_principle: The Court closed the petition because, in view of its order in the related civil appeal, the petition did not survive.

predicates.contempt_proceeding: A petition alleging contempt is pending before the Court.
predicates.related_appeal_order_makes_petition_non_: An order in a related appeal leaves no surviving matter for the contempt petition to address.

issues.definition: When an order in a related appeal leaves a contempt petition with no surviving matter, the petition is closed.
